documents.unit: Office of the University Provost (recommended language, hosted by School of Life Sciences Teaching and Learning Center)
documents.title: Syllabus and Policies for Generative AI (student considerations + Provost Recommended Language, three tiers)
tiers: Circumstantially permitted with explicit permission only
documents.summary: A School of Life Sciences TLC page reproducing the Provost's recommended syllabus language. It gives student considerations (verification, citation, privacy) and three sample statements for instructors to choose from.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'it is essential that instructors clearly communicate expectations' and offers 'three distinct approaches' (generally permitted, permitted with explicit permission only, no use); it sets no single rule, so delegates with three tiers.

units.why: The opening says ASU 'seeks to balance the potential of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to support learning with the need for academic integrity'; it is a framing principle for the guidance, so P56 (institution-level purpose), informs, neutral.
units.anchor: seeks to balance the potential of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to support learning with

units.why: 'it is essential that instructors clearly communicate expectations' is a duty on instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus, so P09 with modality must (essential), phase course-start.
units.anchor: it is essential that instructors clearly communicate expectations for student use of generative AI in

units.why: 'each course has unique goals and values' is the stated reason the decision about AI belongs to each course, so P04 (instructor/course sets the rule) rather than P09, which is coded from the other half of the sentence.
units.anchor: Because each course has unique goals and values
units.policy: Because each course has unique goals and values, expectations for student use of generative AI are set by the instructor for the course.

units.why: 'Instructors may wish to share some or all of the following considerations with students' makes sharing student-facing considerations optional for instructors; it is about communicating expectations (P09), modality may.
units.anchor: Instructors may wish to share some or all of the following considerations with students.

units.why: 'Do not use AI if it does not align with the assignment's purpose' ties permission to each assignment's purpose, which is assignment-level setting (P04); modality must-not; it restricts use to aligned assignments.
units.anchor: Do not use AI if it does not align with the assignment’s purpose.

units.why: 'Effective use requires thoughtful prompting and revision' advises on using AI effectively; closest type is P44 (effective AI use as a skill), though it is framed as a limit, so informs.
units.anchor: Effective use requires thoughtful prompting and revision.

units.why: 'Do not assume outputs are correct. Students are responsible for verifying facts, data, and sources' says AI output can be inaccurate and must be verified, which is P31.
units.anchor: Do not assume outputs are correct. Students are responsible for verifying facts, data, and sources

units.why: 'Students are responsible for properly citing and acknowledging any use of generative AI' is a duty to disclose/cite AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for properly citing and acknowledging any use of generative AI.

units.why: 'Include a brief disclosure describing how AI was used and what prompts were used' requires the prompts as part of the disclosure; P25 (specific details of the citation) fits better than P24 because it names prompts.
units.anchor: Include a brief disclosure describing how AI was used and what prompts were used.

units.why: 'Failure to do so may violate academic integrity policies' makes non-disclosure a violation, which is P28 (rather than P36, since the violation specifically is failing to disclose).
units.anchor: Failure to do so may violate academic integrity policies.

units.why: 'The information entered into prompts may be retained by some generative AI tools and service providers' is a privacy fact warning that prompts are stored, P50, informs.
units.anchor: may be retained by some generative AI tools and service providers

units.why: 'Do not include personal, sensitive, or confidential information in AI prompts' protects personal data, P50, must-not.
units.anchor: Do not include personal, sensitive, or confidential information in AI prompts.

units.why: 'follow all ASU technology use guidelines and information security expectations' when logged in with an ASU account is a data-protection and institutional-tool duty, P50.
units.anchor: follow all ASU technology use guidelines and information security expectations

units.why: 'Adhere to all FERPA laws and expectations related to student privacy' is a privacy duty, P50.
units.anchor: Adhere to all FERPA laws and expectations related to student privacy.

units.why: 'Do not disclose proprietary code, research data, or other information sensitive' bars entering protected institutional information into AI; it is a data-protection rule (P50) rather than P20, because it is about sensitive data not assignment specs.
units.anchor: Do not disclose proprietary code, research data, or other information sensitive to ASU research or

units.why: 'strongly encouraged to use ChatGPT Edu' recommends the university-licensed tool, which is the sanctioned-tool type P17 (the data-security reasoning is in a later unit).
units.anchor: strongly encouraged to use

units.why: 'available to ASU students at no cost through a university agreement' is an access/cost fact, P51.
units.anchor: available to ASU students at no cost through a university agreement
units.policy: ChatGPT Edu is available to ASU students at no cost through a university agreement.

units.why: 'ensures that student data is stored securely and is not used to train OpenAI's models' describes the privacy protection of the licensed tool, P50 (vetted-tool preference), informs.
units.anchor: student data is stored securely and is not used to train OpenAI’s models

units.why: The sentence 'Sample syllabi statements for three distinct approaches are provided below' introduces three named options (generally permitted, permitted with explicit permission only, none permitted), i.e. explicit tiers, P05.
units.anchor: Sample syllabi statements for three distinct approaches are provided below

units.why: Tier 1 language says AI 'is generally welcome [encouraged/required] in this class', a default permit/encourage rule (P02).
units.anchor: is generally welcome [encouraged/required] in this class

units.why: 'Examples of ways that AI tools can be used include [brainstorming, drafting, editing, and revising assignments]' lists permitted uses including brainstorming, fitting P15 best (the list is broader, but brainstorming is first).
units.anchor: Examples of ways that AI tools can be used include [brainstorming, drafting, editing, and revising

units.why: 'You must inform the instructor when you have used an AI tool' requires disclosure of AI use, P24.
units.anchor: You must inform the instructor when you have used an AI tool.

units.why: 'Any submitted course assignment that does not explicitly articulate how generative AI was used will be assumed to have been created entirely without its use' sets a consequence of nondisclosure (treated as no AI use), P28.
units.anchor: does not explicitly articulate how generative AI was used will be assumed to have been

units.why: 'Using AI tools to generate content without proper acknowledgement will be considered a violation of the ASU Academic Integrity Policy' classifies it as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: without proper acknowledgement will be considered a violation of the ASU Academic Integrity Policy

units.why: 'If you have any questions about what is permitted, please contact the instructor to discuss before submitting your work' tells unsure students to ask the instructor first, P10.
units.anchor: please contact the instructor to discuss before submitting your work

units.why: Tier 2 says 'Certain assignments in this course permit or expect' AI use, so AI permission is set assignment by assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Certain assignments in this course permit or expect the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered

units.why: 'Use of generative AI tools in any other context within this course will be considered a violation' states the fallback: AI outside the permitted assignments is prohibited, P06 (it also is misconduct, P36, but the fallback rule is the main point).
units.anchor: Use of generative AI tools in any other context within this course will be considered

units.why: 'The instructor will provide specific instructions on how to utilize generative AI tools for these assignments, as well as how to include appropriate attribution' commits instructors to state per-assignment AI instructions, P09.
units.anchor: The instructor will provide specific instructions on how to utilize generative AI tools for these

units.why: 'The instructor should clearly specify in the syllabus and/or the assignment prompts the allowable generative AI use for each assignment' is a syllabus-statement duty, P09.
units.anchor: clearly specify in the syllabus and/or the assignment prompts the allowable generative AI use for

units.why: Tier 3 states work 'will be created without the use of generative AI' including drafts and brainstorming, a default ban on graded work, P01.
units.anchor: will be created without the use of generative AI

units.why: 'for generating student-attributed content is not permitted in this class' bans AI-generated submitted content across reports, posts, portfolios; P19 (producing the submitted work) is the best fit alongside the blanket P01 unit above.
units.anchor: for generating student-attributed content is not permitted in this class

units.why: 'will be considered a violation of the ASU Academic Integrity Policy' for the no-AI tier classifies use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: The use of these generative AI tools on assignments will be considered a violation

units.why: 'The instructor should consider whether grammar/style-checking software (e.g., Grammarly) is allowable' is guidance to decide separately on writing-assistance tools, P18.
units.anchor: consider whether grammar/style-checking software (e.g., Grammarly) is allowable

units.why: 'inform students how to respond if a group member is explicitly using generative AI' is a group-work rule that fits no listed type (P45 is about AI as collaborator, not a teammate's AI use).
units.anchor: inform students how to respond if a group member is explicitly using generative AI
units.uncovered_note: Instructors tell students how to respond when a group-project teammate uses generative AI.

documents.title: Teaching and learning with generative AI
documents.summary: The Provost's generative AI page mostly promotes ASU's licensed platforms (CreateAI Builder, ChatGPT EDU) for faculty and staff and links to teaching webinars. It contains almost no student-facing rule text.
documents.stance_why: The page encourages faculty to adopt AI platforms ('We recommend that faculty and staff develop teaching and learning experiences in CreateAI Builder') but sets no rule for student AI use, so delegates.

units.why: 'ASU's approach to artificial intelligence is rooted in Principled Innovation' with 'use AI thoughtfully and responsibly' is the institution-level framing, P56.
units.anchor: rooted in Principled Innovation

units.why: 'AI can enhance your teaching and enrich the student experience' welcomes AI use in teaching, a default pro-AI stance, P02, directed at faculty.
units.anchor: AI can enhance your teaching and enrich the student experience.

units.why: 'Explore the Learning Design Suite, which offers AI-driven tools ... to help streamline course planning, syllabus development, quiz generators' points instructors to AI for their own teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: AI-driven tools built for instructional designers and faculty to help streamline course planning, syllabus development,

units.why: CreateAI Builder 'enables faculty and staff to develop FERPA-compliant AI-powered projects', describing a university-provided tool, P17.
units.anchor: enables faculty and staff to develop FERPA-compliant AI-powered projects

units.why: 'assess bias using the Ethical AI Engine' describes bias screening of outputs, a bias concern, P53, informs.
units.anchor: assess bias using the Ethical AI Engine

units.why: 'access robust data for evaluation and efficacy research' says the platform supplies data for studying efficacy, P55.
units.anchor: access robust data for evaluation and efficacy research

units.why: 'Data is securely maintained within the ASU infrastructure, ensuring both privacy and transparency' is a privacy assurance for the vetted platform, P50.
units.anchor: Data is securely maintained within the ASU infrastructure

units.why: 'We recommend that faculty and staff develop teaching and learning experiences in CreateAI Builder' recommends a sanctioned tool, P17, should.
units.anchor: We recommend that faculty and staff develop teaching and learning experiences in CreateAI Builder

units.why: 'If you've used your @asu.edu email for a ChatGPT account that mixes personal and professional work, do not merge it' protects data/account separation for faculty, P50.
units.anchor: do not merge it

units.why: 'Only merge if your content is work-related and contains no HIPAA or restricted data' limits what may be merged to protect restricted data, P50.
units.anchor: Only merge if your content is work-related and contains no HIPAA or restricted data.

units.why: 'You are not required to join the ChatGPT EDU workspace' keeps use optional for staff, an access/choice point, P51.
units.anchor: You are not required to join the ChatGPT EDU workspace.

units.why: 'Student participation is optional ... Use CreateAI builder instead' keeps student use of a course tool optional with an alternative, P51.
units.anchor: Student participation is optional

units.why: 'Generative AI is a type of artificial intelligence that can create new content' defines the term, P61.
units.anchor: Generative AI is a type of artificial intelligence that can create new content

units.why: 'this website will be updated with resources for the ASU community' says the guidance is ongoing and will change, P54.
units.anchor: this website will be updated with resources for the ASU community

units.why: 'offering recommendations and guidelines on how to prevent its misuse' states the purpose of the guidance, balancing benefits and misuse, P56.
units.anchor: embraces its benefits while offering recommendations and guidelines on how to prevent its misuse

units.why: 'If you have feedback about these resources ... please provide it' invites feedback, P54.
units.anchor: If you have feedback about these resources

units.why: The Provost 'invites you to watch the Generative AI Teaching Conversation recordings', which are faculty learning events, P63.
units.anchor: invites you to watch the Generative AI Teaching Conversation recordings

units.why: 'reframing the conversation from cheating to focusing on how AI is already used in education' states a principle about approaching AI and integrity, P56.
units.anchor: reframing the conversation from cheating to focusing on how AI is already used in education

documents.title: Guidelines and resources (AI guidelines and policies, Digital Trust guidelines)
documents.summary: An index page from the AI site that links to Digital Trust guidelines, the list of vetted tools and related university policies. Its own text is brief and concerns data privacy, tool approval and career use.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no stance on student AI use; it only tells readers to 'review the AI Digital Trust guidelines' and lists approved tools, so delegates.

units.why: 'approved for use at the departmental level' with 'completed the ASU VITRA process' identifies vetted tools for departments, P50 (prefer vetted tools).
units.anchor: AI tools that have completed the ASU VITRA process and are approved for use at

units.why: 'If a department would like to use these tools, their department can submit an assessment request' sets the process for departments to adopt tools, P65 (institutional review of AI tools).
units.anchor: their department can submit an assessment request in accordance with their standard process

units.why: 'Before using any AI tools, please review the AI Digital Trust guidelines' on privacy, copyright and IP is a data and IP responsibility, P50.
units.anchor: Before using any AI tools, please review the AI Digital Trust guidelines

units.why: The guidelines were assembled 'to identify appropriate considerations for the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI) at ASU', an institution-level framework, P56.
units.anchor: identify appropriate considerations for the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI) at ASU

units.why: 'we must be aware of the potential risks, including the inadvertent disclosure of proprietary or confidential institutional data' warns about data exposure, P50.
units.anchor: inadvertent disclosure of proprietary or confidential institutional data

units.why: 'Generative AI can offer a great starting point when it comes to research. It can help you explore careers ... prepare for an interview and even tailor your resume' recommends AI for career preparation, P44.
units.anchor: It can help you explore careers relating to your interests and job searching methods, prepare

units.why: 'please review our brand execution guidelines to ensure your work is in alignment with ASU policies' covers brand compliance of AI-made content, which fits no listed type.
units.anchor: please review our brand execution guidelines to ensure your work is in alignment with ASU
units.uncovered_note: AI-assisted work should comply with ASU enterprise brand guidelines.

documents.unit: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, Instruction Junction
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Resources and Guidelines
documents.summary: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences page sets principles: units and faculty decide whether student AI use is permitted, state it in syllabi, and treat AI under academic integrity. It also says detectors are unreliable and suspicion alone does not start a formal investigation.
documents.stance_why: The Dean's Office 'encourages academic units and faculty to determine whether student use ... is permitted or prohibited', so the college sets no stance of its own and delegates.

units.why: 'encourages academic units and faculty to determine whether student use of generative AI/ChatGPT in their courses is permitted or prohibited' hands the decision to units and faculty, P04.
units.anchor: to determine whether student use of generative AI/ChatGPT in their courses is permitted or prohibited

units.why: 'to state this and any parameters in your syllabi, announcements, and assignment instructions' asks units and faculty to communicate AI rules in writing, P09 (the decision itself is coded in the previous unit).
units.anchor: to state this and any parameters in your syllabi, announcements, and assignment instructions

units.why: 'faculty should include the ASU Academic Integrity policy in their syllabi, including copyright and plagiarism verbiage' is a syllabus content duty tied to integrity, P09.
units.anchor: faculty should include the ASU Academic Integrity policy in their syllabi

units.why: 'The use of Generative AI/ChatGPT falls within ASU's Academic Integrity policies and processes' places AI misuse under integrity processes, P36.
units.anchor: falls within ASU's Academic Integrity policies and processes

units.why: 'faculty should emphasize that students must cite any borrowed content sources' directs instructors to tell students to cite, P24 (instructor-facing).
units.anchor: faculty should emphasize that students must cite any borrowed content sources

units.why: 'if students use generative AI, they should cite it' is a disclosure/citation expectation, P24.
units.anchor: if students use generative AI, they should cite it

units.why: 'ensure any AI-generated citations are correct, as generative AI tools are notorious for listing nonsensical citations' warns to verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: ensure any AI-generated citations are correct

units.why: 'The accuracy of AI detection tools is not reliable' says detectors should not be relied on, P39.
units.anchor: The accuracy of AI detection tools is not reliable

units.why: Results 'should be used for nothing more than a starting point for a conversation between faculty and the student', which is the talk-first rule, P57 (P39 is coded in the prior unit).
units.anchor: nothing more than a starting point for a conversation between faculty and the student

units.why: 'ASU administration has not recommended any specific tools or apps to detect the use of AI' states no detector is endorsed, P39.
units.anchor: ASU administration has not recommended any specific tools or apps to detect the use of

units.why: 'Suspected use of Generative AI in coursework is not sufficient evidence to begin a formal Academic Integrity investigation' limits escalation on suspicion alone; P57 (talk first) fits better than P39 because it concerns what must happen before escalation.
units.anchor: Suspected use of Generative AI in coursework is not sufficient evidence to begin a formal

units.why: 'we recommend faculty document their expectations early and often, and have open dialogs with students' advises communicating expectations repeatedly, P09.
units.anchor: we recommend faculty document their expectations early and often
